subject.title: fix: provider usage accounting, retry/overflow classification, and output clamping

question: Should omitted Anthropic `maxRetries` continue to inherit the SDK default for direct provider-package callers, or should the public provider contract intentionally change to disable SDK retries globally?
rationale: The branch currently changes an existing dependency-backed default for every package caller to solve retry stacking in the OpenClaw application; choosing the permanent owner boundary and compatibility contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve package behavior
options.body: Keep `maxRetries` undefined in the provider package and pass `0` from the OpenClaw-owned caller that already applies the outer retry policy.

options.title: Change the provider contract
options.body: Keep the global zero-retry default only with explicit maintainer approval, compatibility documentation, and coverage for direct package consumers.

recommendation.title: Preserve package behavior
recommendation.body: Keep `maxRetries` undefined in the provider package and pass `0` from the OpenClaw-owned caller that already applies the outer retry policy.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the provider package's established retry semantics and its relationship to the Anthropic SDK contract.
